prompt:
Commercial advertising can stimulate business activity and employment, but its critics believe it can also encourage social dissatisfaction and harmful comparisons.

Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Advertising is an unavoidable part of the modern world, serving as a powerful tool for businesses to reach consumers. While many argue that commercial campaigns are essential for economic growth and job creation, others contend that they foster toxic social comparisons and widespread discontent. In my view, although advertising is an undeniable economic driver, its psychological toll is severe enough to warrant stricter industry regulations.

On the one hand, the economic benefits of commercial advertising are substantial. Marketing drives consumer demand, which in turn fuels production and innovation. When businesses successfully sell their products or services through advertising, they generate revenue that allows them to expand. This expansion directly translates into job creation across various sectors, from manufacturing and logistics to the creative agencies that design the campaigns themselves. Without advertising, new companies would struggle to enter the market, and economic stagnation would likely follow.

On the other hand, critics rightly point out the negative social consequences of relentless marketing. To sell products, advertisers frequently manufacture a sense of inadequacy in the consumer, presenting idealized versions of beauty, wealth, and happiness. This constant exposure to unattainable lifestyles can lead to deep-seated social dissatisfaction. People often compare their everyday realities to the curated, flawless lives shown in commercials, which can result in lowered self-esteem, anxiety, and the pursuit of material goods they cannot afford, ultimately driving individuals into debt.

In conclusion, advertising acts as a double-edged sword. It is undeniably a cornerstone of robust economies, providing employment and keeping businesses afloat. However, the systematic promotion of unrealistic lifestyles causes genuine psychological harm. I believe that while we cannot eliminate commercial advertising without damaging the economy, governments and regulatory bodies must enforce stricter standards to curb manipulative tactics and promote more authentic, responsible representations in the media.
expectations: Assess support for the proposed intervention; no fixed band

prompt: Some people think cities should spend more on public transport, while others favour building more roads. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
I think cities should build more roads. Roads are good because people can use them. I use a road when I go to the shops and my brother uses a road when he goes to work. This shows that roads are important. Without roads people would have problems and the city would not be good.

There are many cars in cities. People like cars because they are useful and comfortable. A car can take a family to different places. Families sometimes go to a park and sometimes visit relatives. Roads help them do these things. If there are more roads, there are more places where cars can go. I think that is a good thing for the people who live in the city.

Money is also important. Governments have money and they should spend it on important things. Roads are important things, so they should spend money on roads. Some roads are old and some roads are new. The old roads should be better and the new roads should be good too. Everyone wants a good city and I also want a good city. This is why I agree with building roads.

There are different opinions about cities. Different people want different things, and this is normal. I have explained my opinion because I think roads are useful. A useful thing is something that people need in their lives. People need to go to work, to go shopping and to visit their families. All of these activities are important to them.

In conclusion, I think more roads are a good idea. Roads are important for cars and people use cars every day. The government should listen to people and build good roads in the city.

prompt: Some people think cities should spend more on public transport, while others favour building more roads. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Cities are becoming bigger and transport is an important subject for many people. Some people want governments to spend money on buses and trains, while other people prefer more roads. I think both ideas have benefits, but public transport should receive more attention.

On the one hand, building roads can be helpful. Many people have cars and they want to travel to work quickly. If a city builds a new road, drivers have another route to use. This can make travel easier for some families. Roads are also needed by businesses because they move products between different places. A shop needs deliveries and a restaurant needs fresh food. Therefore, roads are important for the local economy and should not be forgotten when a government makes its plans.

On the other hand, public transport is useful for people who do not have a car. Students and older people often use buses. If the service is cheap, they can travel without spending too much money. Trains can also carry a lot of people at the same time. This may help with traffic because fewer people need to drive. Public transport can also be better for the environment, which is an important issue in modern cities. For these reasons, there are several advantages to spending more money on it.

In my opinion, public transport should be the main priority, although roads are necessary too. Governments need to think carefully about the needs of local people and make a fair decision. It is difficult to please everyone because different people have different opinions. However, with a good plan the city can become a better place to live.

In conclusion, both roads and public transport have useful roles. I prefer more investment in public transport because it can help many people, but some money should still be available for roads.
expectations: Generalised support and weakly justified preference

prompt: Some people think cities should spend more on public transport, while others favour building more roads. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Growing cities must decide whether to expand roads or improve public transport. Both investments can serve legitimate needs, but I favour prioritising frequent, reliable buses and trains in densely populated areas while maintaining essential road access elsewhere.

Supporters of new roads point to journeys that public transport cannot easily replace. A delivery company serving scattered villages needs direct access to shops, and an ambulance cannot wait for a scheduled service. Where a missing connection forces these vehicles through residential streets, a carefully located road can reduce dangerous traffic near homes. Road investment is therefore useful when it addresses an identifiable access problem rather than simply promising that every driver will travel faster.

In dense urban districts, however, improving public transport generally provides a more durable response to congestion. A bus carrying forty passengers requires much less road space than forty separate cars. If buses arrive frequently and have protected lanes, commuters can reasonably leave their cars at home without losing control over their arrival times. This also helps residents who cannot drive: a worker with a low income gains access to jobs beyond walking distance without having to purchase and maintain a vehicle. The benefit is thus both reduced pressure on streets and wider access to employment.

My preference depends on making the alternative practical. Purchasing new buses alone achieves little if they remain trapped in the same traffic or stop running before evening shifts finish. Cities should first identify busy travel corridors, protect bus priority and fund dependable services throughout the working day. They should then monitor passenger numbers and journey times, adjusting routes that fail to connect people with destinations. Essential road repairs and targeted links can continue alongside this programme.

In conclusion, roads remain necessary for emergency access, deliveries and dispersed communities. Nevertheless, cities should give priority to usable public transport where many people travel along shared routes. This approach links spending to the kind of journey it can improve instead of treating either investment as a universal solution.
